    (d : Cfg (k + 2) Bool (Σ key, h1RoundPh k key) x)
    (entry : d.state = some ⟨.entry, ()⟩) (rel : h1RoundRep tr c d) :
    d = h1At (h1Data c (tableBitsK tr) (outputSummary c.output) (unaryFin q) 0 0 d.output) .entry () := by
  obtain ⟨input, bank, table, summary, tableHome, stateHome⟩ := rel
  simp only [hq, Option.map_some, Option.getD_some] at summary
  apply Cfg.ext
  · exact entry
  · exact input
  · funext j
    refine Fin.addCases (fun i => ?_) (fun i => ?_) j
    · simpa only [h1At, Cfg.mapState, h1Data, Fin.addCases_left] using (bank i).1
    · fin_cases i
      · simpa [h1At, Cfg.mapState, h1Data, h1TableTape] using table
      · simpa [h1At, Cfg.mapState, h1Data, h1SummaryTape] using summary
  · funext j
    refine Fin.addCases (fun i => ?_) (fun i => ?_) j
    · simpa only [h1At, Cfg.mapState, h1Data, Fin.addCases_left] using (bank i).2
    · fin_cases i
      · simpa [h1At, Cfg.mapState, h1Data, h1TableTape] using tableHome
      · simpa [h1At, Cfg.mapState, h1Data, h1SummaryTape] using stateHome
  · rfl

/-- **Promotion candidate (host H2, step block; machine-library-design.md §14).**
One finite physical machine `h1RoundFinTM k`, whose control depends only on
`k`, realizes one transition of any canonized `k`-tape table. `h1RoundRep`
fully specifies the seam. The table and unary state are data, never control.
The source action is applied even when its successor is `none`; the block
then reaches the separate live halt exit, after restoring both auxiliaries.

The bound is `50 * (|table| + 1)`. Every simulated head stays at either its
start or its action endpoint, at distance at most one. Every auxiliary head
stays within the same linear bound and returns home. Physical output is
silent at every intermediate time; simulated emission updates the summary.
The strict interior visits neither the continuation anchor nor the halt exit.

**Proof sketch.** Unpack the representation and invoke the complete canonical
round. Output-prefix monotonicity gives silence throughout. The phase window
and the public action head bound give the mirrored envelope. Summing the
public unit step bound gives the auxiliary envelope. The input clamp handles
both boundary blanks. No space ledger or alternative trace is constructed. -/
private theorem h1Round_effect {k n : ℕ} {x : List Bool}
    (tr : Fin (n + 1) → Option Bool → (Fin k → Option Bool) → Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1)))
    (c : Cfg k Bool (Fin (n + 1)) x) (q : Fin (n + 1)) (hq : c.state = some q)
    (d : Cfg (k + 2) Bool (Σ key, h1RoundPh k key) x)
    (entry : d.state = some ⟨.entry, ()⟩) (rel : h1RoundRep tr c d) :
    let a := tr q c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols
    ∃ T, 0 < T ∧ T ≤ 50 * ((tableBitsK tr).length + 1) ∧
      let e := (h1RoundTM k).runFrom d T
      e.state = some (h1RoundExit k a.state.isSome) ∧ h1RoundRep tr (a.apply c) e ∧
      e.workTapeSymbols (h1SummaryTape k) = summaryEmit (d.workTapeSymbols (h1SummaryTape k)) a.output ∧
      (∀ u, 0 < u → u < T → ∃ s, ((h1RoundTM k).runFrom d u).state = some s ∧
        s ≠ ⟨.entry, ()⟩ ∧ s ≠ ⟨.halt, ()⟩) ∧
      (∀ u ≤ T, ((h1RoundTM k).runFrom d u).output = d.output) ∧
      (∀ u ≤ T,
        let f := (h1RoundTM k).runFrom d u
        (f.inputPos = d.inputPos ∨ f.inputPos = e.inputPos) ∧
        |(f.inputPos.val : ℤ) - d.inputPos.val| ≤ 1 ∧
        (∀ i : Fin k, f.workTapePos (Fin.castAdd 2 i) = d.workTapePos (Fin.castAdd 2 i) ∨
          f.workTapePos (Fin.castAdd 2 i) = e.workTapePos (Fin.castAdd 2 i)) ∧
        ∀ j : Fin (k + 2), |f.workTapePos j - d.workTapePos j| ≤
          if j.val < k then 1 else (50 * ((tableBitsK tr).length + 1) : ℕ)) ∧
      ∀ j : Fin (k + 2), k ≤ j.val → d.workTapePos j = 0 ∧ e.workTapePos j = 0 := by
  let a := tr q c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols
  have canonical := h1RoundRep_entry tr c q hq d entry rel
  obtain ⟨T, positive, bound, run, cut, window⟩ := h1Round_canonical tr c q d.output
  rw [← canonical] at run cut window
  refine ⟨T, positive, bound, ?_, ?_, ?_, cut, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [run]
    rfl
  · rw [run]
    simp [h1RoundRep, h1Data, Cfg.mapState, Action.apply, h1TableTape, h1SummaryTape]
  · have old : d.workTapeSymbols (h1SummaryTape k) = outputSummary c.output := by
      rw [canonical]
      simp [h1At, h1Data, Cfg.mapState, Cfg.workTapeSymbols, h1SummaryTape, h1SummaryState]
    rw [run, old]
    simpa only [h1Data, Cfg.mapState, Cfg.workTapeSymbols, h1SummaryTape,
      Fin.addCases_right, show (1 : Fin 2) ≠ 0 from by decide, ↓reduceIte, h1SummaryState] using
      (outputSummary_append c.output a.output)
  · intro u hu
    have lo := (h1RoundTM k).output_prefix d (Nat.zero_le u)
    have hi := (h1RoundTM k).output_prefix d hu
    rw [run] at hi
    exact hi.eq_of_length_le lo.length_le
  · intro u hu
    have frame := window u hu
    have finalInput : ((h1RoundTM k).runFrom d T).inputPos = (a.apply c).inputPos := by rw [run]; rfl
    have finalHead (i : Fin k) : ((h1RoundTM k).runFrom d T).workTapePos (Fin.castAdd 2 i) =
        (a.apply c).workTapePos i := by rw [run]; simp only [h1Data, Cfg.mapState, Fin.addCases_left]; rfl
    have inputStep : |((a.apply c).inputPos.val : ℤ) - c.inputPos.val| ≤ 1 := by
      change |((moveInputPos c.inputPos a.inputTape).val : ℤ) - c.inputPos.val| ≤ 1
      apply abs_le.mpr
      have hp := c.inputPos.isLt
      cases h : a.inputTape <;> simp only [moveInputPos, SignType.cast] <;>
        split <;> simp <;> omega
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa only [rel.1, finalInput] using frame.1
    · rw [rel.1]
      rcases frame.1 with start | finish
      · rw [start]; simp
      · rw [finish]; exact inputStep
    · intro i
      simpa only [(rel.2.1 i).2, finalHead i] using frame.2 i
    · intro j
      by_cases hj : j.val < k
      · let i : Fin k := ⟨j.val, hj⟩
        have ji : j = Fin.castAdd 2 i := Fin.ext rfl
        rw [if_pos hj, ji, (rel.2.1 i).2]
        rcases frame.2 i with start | finish
        · rw [start]; simp
        · rw [finish]; exact workTapePos_apply_le a c i
      · rw [if_neg hj]
        exact (h1Run_headBound (h1RoundTM k) d u j).trans (by omega)
  · intro j hj
    have home (e : Cfg (k + 2) Bool (Σ key, h1RoundPh k key) x)
        (ht : e.workTapePos (h1TableTape k) = 0) (hs : e.workTapePos (h1SummaryTape k) = 0) : e.workTapePos j = 0 := by
      have casesAux : j = h1TableTape k ∨ j = h1SummaryTape k := by
        have limit := j.isLt
        have indices : j.val = k ∨ j.val = k + 1 := by omega
        rcases indices with h | h
        · left; apply Fin.ext; simpa [h1TableTape] using h
        · right; apply Fin.ext; simpa [h1SummaryTape] using h
      rcases casesAux with rfl | rfl
      · exact ht
      · exact hs
    refine ⟨home d rel.2.2.2.2.1 rel.2.2.2.2.2, ?_⟩
    apply home
    · rw [run]; simp [h1Data, Cfg.mapState, h1TableTape]
    · rw [run]; simp [h1Data, Cfg.mapState, h1SummaryTape]

/-- **The uniform bounded-acceptance simulator** (spec, fill pending — batch
B5a): one finite binary machine and one degree such that, on
`⟨⟨bits t, α⟩, x⟩`, the machine answers `[true]` if the machine `α` denotes
halts on `x` with output exactly `[true]` within `t` steps, and `[false]`
otherwise, within `d · (|α| + |x| + t + 1)^d` steps. [AB09, §1.4.1, Theorem 1.9,
time-bounded form; Example 3.6(3)'s uniformity]

**Proof sketch.** Parse the nested input onto tapes: the deadline word
`bits t` on a counter tape, `α` on a table tape, `x` on a buffer tape. Canonize
`α` in place by `Turing.MachineFormat.exists_polyCanonizer` through
`Turing.FinTM.exists_installCallTM`; by `F.serialize_eq` the table is
`serializeK (F.machine (F.decode α))`, of length at most
`max |α| |F.serialize F.fallback|` (`Turing.CodeFormat.serialize_decode_length_le`).
The body is **one step block**: for the current simulated state (unary on a
state tape), input read and `k` work reads, seek the record at index
`q · 3^(k+1) + rank(inp, w)`, read it by the `Turing.codeReadActionK` grammar
(`Turing.codeReadActionK_append`), apply it to `k` mirrored work tapes and the
simulated input head, and update a finite output summary (empty, exactly
`[true]`, other) instead of emitting. Its cost is at most `B · (|table| + 1)`,
independent of `t`, `x` and the tape contents. The block reads the simulated
input through its own input head and is hosted on the buffer by
`Turing.vhostEmitTM` (`Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom`); the clock is
`Turing.counterLoopTM` over `bits t` (`Turing.counterLoopTM_run_done`,
`Turing.counterLoopTM_run_escape`), a simulated halt being the live exit. At
`done` the simulated machine is live after `t` steps, so the answer is `false`;
at `escape` it has halted within `t`, and the answer is the summary's
`[true]` test. The ledger: polynomial startup, `t` rounds of at most
`B · (|table| + 1)` (`Turing.counterLoop_time_le`), and the verdict, all at most
`d · (|α| + |x| + t + 1)^d`.

**Fill appendix (B5a partial, D4).** The seven output-summary/clock declarations
have moved from `Codes2Tape` and are generalized to arbitrary tape and state
counts. `summaryClock_accepts` identifies the inclusive-deadline predicate;
`summaryClock_zero` handles zero. These are semantic specifications only.
The one physical step block, its relation-level trace, the counter/virtual-input
host assembly, and its ledger remain open; this target retains its admission.

**Fill appendix (B5a H1, selected-record partial).** The private `h1RecordTM`
reads the fixed action fields into finite control and executes them on the
mirrored bank and native input, recording the emission by `summaryEmit`.
`h1Record_read`, `h1Record_execute`, and `h1Record_effect`
prove its framed physical trace, source-action relation, silence, first live
exit, and exact `4k + 5` time bound. Its control depends only on `k`; the
public `codeReadActionK_append` supplies the decoding proof. The table head
is left at the actual successor field. Record lookup, successor installation,
restoration of the round seam, nested-input setup, canonizer installation,
and the complete hosted counter loop remain open. This target keeps its
original admission; these new private components contain no admissions.
Addendum 1 is proved for this component by `h1Record_envelope` and is included
in `h1Record_effect`: only the final payload step moves a mirrored or native
input head, each by at most one; the summary head stays fixed and the table
head advances by at most `4k + 4`. The full round's auxiliary-home restoration
and head envelope remain part of the open step-block construction.

**Fill appendix (H1 continuation, partial; complete generic step block).**
The inherited frontier's items 1–3 are now proved in `h1Round_effect` for the
single finite machine `h1RoundFinTM k`. Its control is independent of the coded
state count. Whole-record lookup follows `tableBitsK`'s exact read order,
executes the inherited fixed payload, installs the variable-length successor,
and restores both auxiliary heads to zero. The relation-level contract includes
a live halt exit after applying the halting action, silence at every prefix,
first-return cuts, a `50 * (|table| + 1)` bound, and the whole-round head envelope.
The unary state shares the summary auxiliary: summary at zero, blank at one,
and the state word at two. This layout preserves the inherited summary cell.
All new helpers are proved without admissions. This partial does not discharge
the headline: nested-input startup and canonizer installation, Z1 hosting and
the counter loop, the joint polynomial ledger, and note 50's physical H1
exact-deadline checks remain. The original statement and pending tag are unchanged.
-/
theorem exists_uniformSimulator :
    ∃ (S : FinTM Bool) (d : ℕ), ∀ (α x : List Bool) (t : ℕ),
      ((F.toFinTM (F.decode α)).ComputesInTime x [true] t →
        S.ComputesInTime (pairEncode (pairEncode (Nat.bits t) α) x) [true]
          (d * (α.length + x.length + t + 1) ^ d)) ∧
      (¬(F.toFinTM (F.decode α)).ComputesInTime x [true] t →
        S.ComputesInTime (pairEncode (pairEncode (Nat.bits t) α) x) [false]
          (d * (α.length + x.length + t + 1) ^ d)) := by
  sorry

end MachineFormat

end Turing
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/CodeFormat.lean (at the gate head) =====

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CodeParser

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Machine-code formats

The shared record and table parser layer for fixed machine serializations.
This factors the one- and two-work-tape constructions of [AB09, §1.4].

## Main definitions

* `Turing.CodeFormat` — a table grammar, its laws and its fallback.
* `Turing.actionBitsK` / `Turing.codeReadActionK` — records for any work-tape count.
* `Turing.CodeTable2` — the shared 27-record two-work-tape table.
* `Turing.oneTapeFormat` — the one-work-tape instance and public decoder wrappers.

## Main results

* `Turing.CodeFormat.decode_serialize_pad` — padded decoding recovers the machine.
* `Turing.CodeFormat.canonical_eq` — scanning computes its canonical serialization.
* `Turing.CodeFormat.numStates_decode_le` — the guarded decoded-size bound.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.4, pp. 19-20.)
-/

namespace Turing


/-! ## Transition records -/

/-- The serialization of a transition record lists the input move, each work-tape write
and move in tape order, the output, and the successor state. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def actionBitsK {k n : ℕ} (a : Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1))) : List Bool :=
  signBits a.inputTape ++
    (List.finRange k).flatMap
      (fun i => optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes i).1 ++ signBits (a.workTapes i).2) ++
    optBoolBits a.output ++ optStateBits a.state

/-- Read an optional work-tape write and its head move. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeReadWork (xs : List Bool) :
    Option ((Option (Option Bool) × SignType) × List Bool) := do
  let (wr, xs) ← codeReadWrite xs
  let (wm, xs) ← codeReadSign xs
  pure ((wr, wm), xs)

/-- Read a transition record with a vector of `k` work-tape actions. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeReadActionK (k n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    Option (Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1)) × List Bool) := do
  let (im, xs) ← codeReadSign xs
  let (ws, xs) ← codeReadVec codeReadWork k xs
  let (out, xs) ← codeReadOutput xs
  let (q, xs) ← codeReadState (n + 1) xs
  pure (⟨im, ws, out, q⟩, xs)

/-- Skip a work-tape write and move, enforcing their field grammar. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeSkipWork (xs : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) :=
  (codeSkipPair (fun _ _ => true) xs).bind (codeSkipPair (fun a b => a || !b))

/-- Skip a transition record for `k` work tapes, checking the successor state bound. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeSkipActionK (k n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) := do
  let xs ← codeSkipPair (fun a b => a || !b) xs
  let xs ← codeSkipRepeat codeSkipWork k xs
  let xs ← codeSkipPair (fun a b => a || !b) xs
  codeSkipState (n + 1) xs

/-- Reading a serialized work-tape action recovers it and leaves the suffix untouched. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadWork_append (p : Option (Option Bool) × SignType) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeReadWork ((optOptBoolBits p.1 ++ signBits p.2) ++ xs) = some (p, xs) := by
  rcases p with ⟨wr, wm⟩
  simp only [codeReadWork, List.append_assoc, codeReadWrite_append, codeReadSign_append,
    bind, Option.bind, pure]

/-- Reading a serialized transition recovers it and leaves the suffix untouched. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadActionK_append {k n : ℕ} (a : Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1))) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeReadActionK k n (actionBitsK a ++ xs) = some (a, xs) := by
  rcases a with ⟨im, ws, out, q⟩
  have hv : ∀ ys, codeReadVec codeReadWork k
      ((List.finRange k).flatMap (fun i => optOptBoolBits (ws i).1 ++ signBits (ws i).2) ++ ys) =
        some (ws, ys) :=
    codeReadVec_append codeReadWork (fun p => optOptBoolBits p.1 ++ signBits p.2)
      codeReadWork_append k ws
  simp only [actionBitsK, List.append_assoc, codeReadActionK, codeReadSign_append, hv,
    codeReadOutput_append, codeReadState_append, bind, Option.bind, pure]

/-- A successful work-tape read consumes exactly the serialization of its result. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadWork_sound (xs : List Bool) (p : Option (Option Bool) × SignType)
    (rest : List Bool) (h : codeReadWork xs = some (p, rest)) :
    xs = (optOptBoolBits p.1 ++ signBits p.2) ++ rest := by
  simp only [codeReadWork, bind, Option.bind_eq_some_iff] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨wr, r₁⟩, h₁, ⟨⟨wm, r₂⟩, h₂, h⟩⟩ := h
  simp only [pure, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
  rw [codeReadWrite_sound xs wr r₁ h₁, codeReadSign_sound r₁ wm r₂ h₂]
  simp [List.append_assoc]

/-- A successful transition read consumes exactly the serialization of its result. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadActionK_sound {k n : ℕ} (xs : List Bool) (a : Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1)))
    (rest : List Bool) (h : codeReadActionK k n xs = some (a, rest)) :
    xs = actionBitsK a ++ rest := by
  simp only [codeReadActionK, bind, Option.bind_eq_some_iff] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨im, r₁⟩, h₁, ⟨⟨ws, r₂⟩, h₂, ⟨⟨out, r₃⟩, h₃, ⟨⟨q, r₄⟩, h₄, h⟩⟩⟩⟩ := h
  simp only [pure, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
  rw [codeReadSign_sound xs im r₁ h₁,
    codeReadVec_sound codeReadWork (fun p => optOptBoolBits p.1 ++ signBits p.2)
      codeReadWork_sound k r₁ ws r₂ h₂,
    codeReadOutput_sound r₂ out r₃ h₃, codeReadState_sound r₃ q r₄ h₄]
  simp [actionBitsK, List.append_assoc]

/-- Erasing the work-tape reader result gives the work-tape skipper. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeEraseWork (xs : List Bool) : (codeReadWork xs).map Prod.snd = codeSkipWork xs := by
  simp only [codeReadWork, codeSkipWork, bind, Option.map_bind, Function.comp_def, pure,
    Option.map_some]
  rw [← codeEraseWrite xs, ← codeErase_bind]
  congr 1; funext p
  simpa only [Option.map_eq_bind, Function.comp_def] using codeEraseSign p.2

/-- Erasing the transition reader result gives the transition skipper. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeEraseActionK (k n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    (codeReadActionK k n xs).map Prod.snd = codeSkipActionK k n xs := by
  have hv (ys : List Bool) :
      (codeReadVec codeReadWork k ys).map Prod.snd = codeSkipRepeat codeSkipWork k ys := by
    rw [codeEraseVec]
    exact congrArg (fun r => codeSkipRepeat r k ys) (funext codeEraseWork)
  simp only [codeReadActionK, codeSkipActionK, bind, Option.map_bind, Function.comp_def, pure,
    Option.map_some]
  rw [← codeEraseSign xs, ← codeErase_bind]
  congr 1; funext p
  rw [← hv p.2, ← codeErase_bind]
  congr 1; funext p
  rw [← codeEraseOutput p.2, ← codeErase_bind]
  congr 1; funext p
  simpa only [Option.map_eq_bind, Function.comp_def] using codeEraseState (n + 1) p.2

/-- Every `k`-work-tape record has at least `4 * k + 5` bits. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** Each work tape contributes four bits. The input move and output contribute
four more, and the successor-state field contributes at least one. -/
lemma codeActionK_length {k n : ℕ} (a : Action k Bool (Fin (n + 1))) :
    4 * k + 5 ≤ (actionBitsK a).length := by
  have hs (s : SignType) : (signBits s).length = 2 := by cases s <;> rfl
  have ho (b : Option Bool) : (optBoolBits b).length = 2 := by
    rcases b with _ | b
    · rfl
    · cases b <;> rfl
  have hw (b : Option (Option Bool)) : (optOptBoolBits b).length = 2 := by
    rcases b with _ | (_ | b)
    · rfl
    · rfl
    · cases b <;> rfl
  have hq : 1 ≤ (optStateBits a.state).length := by
    cases a.state <;>
      simp only [optStateBits, unaryFin, List.length_cons, List.length_append,
        List.length_replicate, List.length_nil] <;> omega
  have hv : 4 * k ≤ ((List.finRange k).flatMap fun i =>
      optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes i).1 ++ signBits (a.workTapes i).2).length := by
    simpa using codeFlatMap_length (List.finRange k)
      (fun i => optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes i).1 ++ signBits (a.workTapes i).2) 4
      (fun i _ => by simp [hs, hw])
  simp only [actionBitsK, List.length_append, hs, ho]
  omega

/-- The work-symbol function reading `w₀` on tape `0` and `w₁` on tape `1`,
for the fixed table enumeration of `Turing.CodeNDTM.serialize`. -/
def workPair (w₀ w₁ : Option Bool) : Fin 2 → Option Bool :=
  fun j => if j = 0 then w₀ else w₁

/-- Serialization of one two-work-tape transition record: the input-head move,
then each work tape's optional write and move in tape order, then the emission
and the successor state — `Turing.actionBits` with a second work-tape record. -/
def actionBits₂ {n : ℕ} (a : Action 2 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) : List Bool :=
  signBits a.inputTape ++
    optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes 0).1 ++ signBits (a.workTapes 0).2 ++
    optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes 1).1 ++ signBits (a.workTapes 1).2 ++
    optBoolBits a.output ++ optStateBits a.state

/-- The fixed one-work-tape serialization agrees with the generic record serialization. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma actionBits_eq_actionBitsK {n : ℕ} (a : Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) :
    actionBits a = actionBitsK a := by
  simp [actionBits, actionBitsK, List.finRange_succ, List.append_assoc]

/-- The fixed two-work-tape serialization agrees with the generic record serialization. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma actionBits₂_eq_actionBitsK {n : ℕ} (a : Action 2 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) :
    actionBits₂ a = actionBitsK a := by
  simp [actionBits₂, actionBitsK, List.finRange_succ, List.append_assoc]

/-- The fixed one-work-tape skipper agrees with the generic skipper at `k = 1`. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeSkipAction_eq_codeSkipActionK (n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeSkipAction n xs = codeSkipActionK 1 n xs := by
  have h1 (ys : List Bool) : codeSkipRepeat codeSkipWork 1 ys = codeSkipWork ys := by
    cases h : codeSkipWork ys <;> simp [codeSkipRepeat, h]
  simp only [codeSkipAction, codeSkipActionK, h1, codeSkipWork, bind, Option.bind_assoc]

/-! ## Table formats -/

/-- A machine-code format specifies a transition-table grammar under the shared
state-count and initial-state header, together with its parser laws and fallback. [AB09, §1.4] -/
structure CodeFormat where
  /-- the coded machines -/
  Code : Type
  /-- the transition table of a machine with `n + 1` states -/
  Table : ℕ → Type
  /-- one less than the number of states -/
  numStates : Code → ℕ
  /-- assemble a machine from its state count, initial state and table -/
  assemble : (n : ℕ) → Fin (n + 1) → Table n → Code
  /-- the format's fixed serialization -/
  serialize : Code → List Bool
  /-- the fixed serialization of a table -/
  tableBits : {n : ℕ} → Table n → List Bool
  /-- the table reader -/
  readTable : (n : ℕ) → List Bool → Option (Table n × List Bool)
  /-- the erased table reader -/
  skipTable : ℕ → List Bool → Option (List Bool)
  /-- the minimum number of table bits per state (the up-front guard constant) -/
  guard : ℕ
  /-- the machine denoted by every malformed string -/
  fallback : Code
  numStates_assemble : ∀ n q t, numStates (assemble n q t) = n
  serialize_assemble : ∀ n q (t : Table n),
    serialize (assemble n q t) = pairEncode n.bits (unaryFin q ++ tableBits t)
  assemble_surj : ∀ M, ∃ n q t, assemble n q t = M
  readTable_append : ∀ n (t : Table n) xs, readTable n (tableBits t ++ xs) = some (t, xs)
  readTable_sound : ∀ n xs (t : Table n) rest,
    readTable n xs = some (t, rest) → xs = tableBits t ++ rest
  readTable_erase : ∀ n xs, (readTable n xs).map Prod.snd = skipTable n xs
  tableBits_length : ∀ n (t : Table n), guard * (n + 1) ≤ (tableBits t).length

namespace CodeFormat

variable (F : CodeFormat)

/-- Parse a machine and retain its all-true padding; check the table-length guard
before reading any state-indexed table entries. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def parseFull (xs : List Bool) : Option (F.Code × List Bool) := do
  let (bits, rest) ← pairDecode xs
  let n := codeBitsNat bits
  if bits ≠ n.bits then none else do
    if F.guard * (n + 1) > rest.length then none else do
      let (q, rest) ← codeReadFin (n + 1) rest
      let (table, rest) ← F.readTable n rest
      if rest.all id then pure (F.assemble n q table, rest) else none

/-- Decode every string, choosing the format's fallback on any malformed input. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def decode (xs : List Bool) : F.Code := ((F.parseFull xs).map Prod.fst).getD F.fallback

/-- Check the same header, table-length guard and padding as the parser,
retaining only the unconsumed suffix. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def scan (xs : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) := do
  let (bits, rest) ← pairDecode xs
  let n := codeBitsNat bits
  if bits ≠ n.bits then none else do
    if F.guard * (n + 1) > rest.length then none else do
      let rest ← codeSkipFin (n + 1) rest
      let rest ← F.skipTable n rest
      if rest.all id then pure rest else none

/-- Return the consumed prefix when scanning succeeds and the fallback's serialization
when scanning fails. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def canonical (xs : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (F.scan xs).casesOn (F.serialize F.fallback) fun tail => xs.take (xs.length - tail.length)

/-- Parsing a serialization followed by true padding recovers the machine and padding. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** The doubled header recovers the canonical state-count bits. The table-length
bound discharges the early guard; the initial-state and table inverse laws recover
the assembled machine and leave the replicated true suffix, which passes the padding test. -/
theorem parseFull_serialize_pad (M : F.Code) (m : ℕ) :
    F.parseFull (F.serialize M ++ List.replicate m true) =
      some (M, List.replicate m true) := by
  obtain ⟨n, q, t, rfl⟩ := F.assemble_surj M
  have hp (a b c : List Bool) : pairEncode a b ++ c = pairEncode a (b ++ c) := by
    simp [pairEncode, List.append_assoc]
  rw [F.serialize_assemble, hp]
  unfold parseFull
  rw [pairDecode_pairEncode]
  dsimp only [bind, Option.bind]
  rw [codeBitsNat_bits]
  simp only [ne_eq, not_true_eq_false, ↓reduceIte]
  have hlen := F.tableBits_length n t
  simp only [List.length_append, List.length_replicate] at *
  rw [if_neg (by omega)]
  simp only [List.append_assoc, codeReadFin_append, F.readTable_append,
    List.all_replicate, id_eq, ite_self, ↓reduceIte, pure]

/-- Decoding a serialization followed by arbitrary true padding recovers the machine. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem decode_serialize_pad (M : F.Code) (m : ℕ) :
    F.decode (F.serialize M ++ List.replicate m true) = M := by
  simp only [decode, parseFull_serialize_pad, Option.map_some, Option.getD_some]

/-- Every successful parse expresses the input as the decoded serialization and suffix. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** Decompose the successful parse and use the field and table soundness equations.
The canonical state-count check reconstructs the doubled header, giving exactly
the machine serialization followed by the retained suffix. -/
theorem parseFull_sound (xs : List Bool) (M : F.Code) (tail : List Bool)
    (h : F.parseFull xs = some (M, tail)) : xs = F.serialize M ++ tail := by
  unfold parseFull at h
  obtain ⟨⟨bits, rest⟩, hp, h⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.mp h
  dsimp only at h
  split at h
  · contradiction
  next hb =>
    have hb : bits = (codeBitsNat bits).bits := not_not.mp hb
    split at h
    · contradiction
    next _ =>
      simp only [bind, Option.bind_eq_some_iff] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨q, r₁⟩, hq, ⟨⟨table, r₂⟩, ht, h⟩⟩ := h
      split at h
      next hpad =>
        simp only [pure, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
        rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
        have htable := F.readTable_sound _ _ _ _ ht
        dsimp only at htable
        rw [F.serialize_assemble, eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode xs bits rest hp,
          codeReadFin_sound rest q r₁ hq, htable]
        simp only [pairEncode, List.append_assoc]
        congr 1
        exact congrArg (List.flatMap fun b : Bool => [b, b]) hb
      · contradiction

/-- The erased scanner returns exactly the suffix retained by the full parser. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** Push suffix projection through the parser's binds and branches. The initial-state
and table erasure laws replace their readers by the corresponding skippers; the
header checks and final padding test are unchanged. -/
theorem scan_full (xs : List Bool) : F.scan xs = (F.parseFull xs).map Prod.snd := by
  simp only [scan, parseFull, bind, Option.map_bind, Function.comp_def]
  congr 1
  funext p
  dsimp only
  split <;> try simp only [Option.map_none]
  split <;> try simp only [Option.map_none, Option.map_bind, Function.comp_def]
  have h (q : Fin (codeBitsNat p.1 + 1) × List Bool) (t : F.Table (codeBitsNat p.1) × List Bool) :
      (if t.2.all id then some (F.assemble (codeBitsNat p.1) q.1 t.1, t.2) else none).map
          Prod.snd = (if t.2.all id then some t.2 else none) := by split <;> rfl
  simp only [pure, h]
  rw [← codeEraseFin _ _, ← codeErase_bind]
  congr 1; funext q
  rw [← F.readTable_erase, ← codeErase_bind]

/-- The scanner-based canonical prefix equals the serialization of the decoded machine. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem canonical_eq (xs : List Bool) : F.canonical xs = F.serialize (F.decode xs) := by
  unfold canonical decode
  rw [scan_full]
  cases h : F.parseFull xs with
  | none => rfl
  | some p =>
    rcases p with ⟨M, tail⟩
    simp only [Option.map_some, Option.getD_some]
    rw [F.parseFull_sound xs M tail h]
    simp

/-- The decoded serialization is no longer than the input or the fixed fallback,
whichever is longer. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem serialize_decode_length_le (α : List Bool) :
    (F.serialize (F.decode α)).length ≤ max α.length (F.serialize F.fallback).length := by
  rw [← F.canonical_eq]
  unfold canonical
  cases F.scan α with
  | none => exact Nat.le_max_right _ _
  | some tail => exact (List.length_take_le' _ _).trans (Nat.le_max_left _ _)

/-- The guarded table-size lower bound for the decoded machine is bounded by the
input length or the fallback length, whichever is larger. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem numStates_decode_le (α : List Bool) :
    F.guard * (F.numStates (F.decode α) + 1) ≤
      max α.length (F.serialize F.fallback).length := by
  have hsize := F.serialize_decode_length_le α
  obtain ⟨n, q, t, h⟩ := F.assemble_surj (F.decode α)
  rw [← h, F.serialize_assemble, length_pairEncode, List.length_append] at hsize
  rw [← h, F.numStates_assemble]
  have htable := F.tableBits_length n t
  omega

/-- A failed full parse decodes to the format's fallback. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem decode_of_parseFull_none (α : List Bool) (h : F.parseFull α = none) :
    F.decode α = F.fallback := by
  simp [decode, h]

/-- A failed table-length guard decodes to the fallback before table recursion. [AB09, §1.4] -/
theorem decode_of_guard_lt (α bits rest : List Bool) (hp : pairDecode α = some (bits, rest))
    (hg : rest.length < F.guard * (codeBitsNat bits + 1)) : F.decode α = F.fallback := by
  simp [decode, parseFull, hp, hg]

end CodeFormat

/-! ## Two-work-tape tables -/

/-- A two-work-tape transition table is indexed by state, input read, and both work reads. [AB09, §1.4] -/
abbrev CodeTable2 (n : ℕ) : Type :=
  Fin (n + 1) → Option Bool → Option Bool → Option Bool → Action 2 Bool (Fin (n + 1))

/-- Serialize all two-work-tape table entries in state, input, work-0, work-1 order. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeTable2Bits {n : ℕ} (t : CodeTable2 n) : List Bool :=
  (List.finRange (n + 1)).flatMap fun q =>
    ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
      ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₀ =>
        ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₁ =>
          actionBitsK (t q inp w₀ w₁)

/-- Read the 27 two-work-tape transition records for every state. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeReadTable2 (n : ℕ) : List Bool → Option (CodeTable2 n × List Bool) :=
  codeReadVec (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadActionK 2 n)))) (n + 1)

/-- Skip the 27 two-work-tape transition records for every state. [AB09, §1.4] -/
def codeSkipTable2 (n : ℕ) : List Bool → Option (List Bool) :=
  codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipActionK 2 n) 3) 3) 3)
    (n + 1)

/-- Reading a serialized two-work-tape table recovers it and leaves the suffix untouched. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadTable2_append {n : ℕ} (t : CodeTable2 n) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeReadTable2 n (codeTable2Bits t ++ xs) = some (t, xs) :=
  codeReadVec_append _ _ (fun _ _ => codeReadSymbols_append _ _
    (fun _ _ => codeReadSymbols_append _ _
      (fun _ _ => codeReadSymbols_append _ _ codeReadActionK_append _ _) _ _) _ _) _ _ _

/-- A successful two-work-tape table read consumes exactly its serialization. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeReadTable2_sound {n : ℕ} (xs : List Bool) (t : CodeTable2 n) (rest : List Bool)
    (h : codeReadTable2 n xs = some (t, rest)) : xs = codeTable2Bits t ++ rest :=
  codeReadVec_sound _ _ (fun _ _ _ => codeReadSymbols_sound _ _
    (fun _ _ _ => codeReadSymbols_sound _ _
      (fun _ _ _ => codeReadSymbols_sound _ _ codeReadActionK_sound _ _ _) _ _ _) _ _ _)
    _ _ _ _ h

/-- Erasing the two-work-tape table reader result gives the corresponding skipper. [AB09, §1.4] -/
lemma codeEraseTable2 (n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    (codeReadTable2 n xs).map Prod.snd = codeSkipTable2 n xs := by
  have ht := codeEraseVec
    (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadActionK 2 n)))) (n + 1) xs
  simp only [codeEraseSymbols, codeEraseActionK] at ht
  exact ht

/-- Every two-work-tape table has at least 351 bits per state. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** Every record has at least 13 bits. Sum this lower bound over each of the
three possible symbols on each of three reads, giving 27 records and 351 bits
per state; then sum over the state enumeration. -/
lemma codeTable2Bits_length {n : ℕ} (t : CodeTable2 n) :
    351 * (n + 1) ≤ (codeTable2Bits t).length := by
  have hr : ∀ a : Action 2 Bool (Fin (n + 1)), 13 ≤ (actionBitsK a).length :=
    fun a => by have := codeActionK_length a; omega
  have h := codeFlatMap_length (List.finRange (n + 1))
    (fun q => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
      ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₀ =>
        ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₁ =>
          actionBitsK (t q inp w₀ w₁)) 351 (by
      intro q _
      have h := codeFlatMap_length ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool))
        (fun inp => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₀ =>
          ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₁ =>
            actionBitsK (t q inp w₀ w₁)) 117 (by
          intro inp _
          have h := codeFlatMap_length ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool))
            (fun w₀ => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w₁ =>
              actionBitsK (t q inp w₀ w₁)) 39 (by
                intro w₀ _
                simpa using codeFlatMap_length
                  ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool))
                  (fun w₁ => actionBitsK (t q inp w₀ w₁)) 13 (fun _ _ => hr _))
          simpa using h)
      simpa using h)
  simpa [codeTable2Bits] using h

/-! ## One-work-tape instance -/

private lemma codeReadActionK_one_append {n : ℕ} (a : Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) (xs : List Bool) :
    codeReadActionK 1 n (actionBits a ++ xs) = some (a, xs) := by
  rw [actionBits_eq_actionBitsK]; exact codeReadActionK_append a xs

private lemma codeReadActionK_one_sound {n : ℕ} (xs : List Bool) (a : Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1)))
    (rest : List Bool) (h : codeReadActionK 1 n xs = some (a, rest)) :
    xs = actionBits a ++ rest := by
  rw [actionBits_eq_actionBitsK]; exact codeReadActionK_sound xs a rest h

private lemma codeEraseActionK_one (n : ℕ) (xs : List Bool) :
    (codeReadActionK 1 n xs).map Prod.snd = codeSkipAction n xs := by
  rw [codeEraseActionK, codeSkipAction_eq_codeSkipActionK]

/-- The one-work-tape `CodeTM` format has nine records per state and guard 81. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** The frozen record serialization is the generic one at one work tape. Nested
vector and symbol-reader laws provide table inversion, soundness and erasure;
summing the nine-bit record bound over the nine records gives guard 81. -/
def oneTapeFormat : CodeFormat where
  Code := CodeTM
  Table := fun n => Fin (n + 1) → Option Bool → Option Bool → Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1))
  numStates := CodeTM.numStates
  assemble := fun n q t => ⟨n, ⟨q, fun s inp w => t s inp (w 0)⟩⟩
  serialize := CodeTM.serialize
  tableBits := fun {n} t => (List.finRange (n + 1)).flatMap fun q =>
    ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
      ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w =>
        actionBits (t q inp w)
  readTable := fun n =>
    codeReadVec (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadActionK 1 n))) (n + 1)
  skipTable := fun n =>
    codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipRepeat (codeSkipAction n) 3) 3) (n + 1)
  guard := 81
  fallback := codeFallback
  numStates_assemble := fun _ _ _ => rfl
  serialize_assemble := fun _ _ _ => rfl
  assemble_surj := by
    rintro ⟨n, q, tr⟩
    refine ⟨n, q, fun s inp w => tr s inp (fun _ => w), ?_⟩
    show CodeTM.mk n ⟨q, fun s inp w => tr s inp (fun _ => w 0)⟩ = CodeTM.mk n ⟨q, tr⟩
    congr 1
    congr 1
    funext s inp w
    apply congrArg (tr s inp)
    funext i
    exact congrArg w (Subsingleton.elim _ _)
  readTable_append := fun _ _ _ =>
    codeReadVec_append _ _ (fun _ _ => codeReadSymbols_append _ _
      (fun _ _ => codeReadSymbols_append _ _ codeReadActionK_one_append _ _) _ _) _ _ _
  readTable_sound := fun _ _ _ _ h =>
    codeReadVec_sound _ _ (fun _ _ _ => codeReadSymbols_sound _ _
      (fun _ _ _ => codeReadSymbols_sound _ _ codeReadActionK_one_sound _ _ _) _ _ _)
      _ _ _ _ h
  readTable_erase := fun n xs => by
    have ht := codeEraseVec (codeReadSymbols (codeReadSymbols (codeReadActionK 1 n))) (n + 1) xs
    simp only [codeEraseSymbols, codeEraseActionK_one] at ht
    exact ht
  tableBits_length := fun n t => by
    have hr : ∀ a : Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1)), 9 ≤ (actionBits a).length := fun a => by
      rw [actionBits_eq_actionBitsK]; have := codeActionK_length a; omega
    have h := codeFlatMap_length (List.finRange (n + 1))
      (fun q => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
        ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w =>
          actionBits (t q inp w)) 81 (by
        intro q _
        have h := codeFlatMap_length ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool))
          (fun inp => ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w =>
            actionBits (t q inp w)) 27 (by
              intro inp _
              simpa using codeFlatMap_length
                ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool))
                (fun w => actionBits (t q inp w)) 9 (fun _ _ => hr _))
        simpa using h)
    simpa using h

/-- Total decoding: every malformed string denotes the fixed fallback. -/
def codeDecode (xs : List Bool) : CodeTM :=
  oneTapeFormat.decode xs

/-- The total decoder satisfies the required exact padded round-trip law. -/
lemma codeDecode_serialize_pad (M : CodeTM) (m : ℕ) :
    codeDecode (M.serialize ++ List.replicate m true) = M :=
  oneTapeFormat.decode_serialize_pad M m

/-- The erased parser: accept exactly the strings the parser accepts, returning only the unconsumed all-true suffix. -/
def codeScan (xs : List Bool) : Option (List Bool) :=
  oneTapeFormat.scan xs

/-- The canonical serialization of the machine a string denotes: the consumed prefix on scanner success, the fallback machine's serialization otherwise. -/
def codeCanonical (xs : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  oneTapeFormat.canonical xs

/-- The suffix scanner computes exactly the fixed serialization of the decoded machine. -/
lemma codeCanonical_eq (xs : List Bool) : codeCanonical xs = (codeDecode xs).serialize :=
  oneTapeFormat.canonical_eq xs

end Turing
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/CounterLoop.lean (at the gate head) =====

```
/-

Authors: Seyoon Ragavan

import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Digits.Defs
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Bool
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Scan
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.SymbolLift

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Machine-construction library: counter-driven loops (§12.7)

The §12.7 increment of the machine-construction library
(`machine-library-design.md` §12.7): a loop whose number of rounds is a
little-endian binary counter **read from a tape**, running a body whose
state lives on **persistent, arbitrarily positioned tapes**. Every public
loop host of `Build/Loop.lean` instead runs a number of rounds fixed by the
input length, between canonical `Turing.Cfg.ofWords` seams. The consumers
are the two-tape uniform machine-code scheme (`Codes2Tape`), the EXPCOM
simulation, the nondeterministic time hierarchy (a fused countdown at
linear overhead) and the space hierarchy's configuration-count clock.

**Status update (§12.8 fill, R8.0b/R8.6).** All contracts in this file are proved.
The expansion proof cites `Turing.writeAdvTM_run_ofCfg` (`Build/Scan`, proved by the §12.8
stream-B fill), so nothing in this file is proved modulo an admission (R8.0b gate round 1,
note F14: doc-only refresh after the combined tree was checked).
**Alphabet update (R8.0b).** The shared loop machinery now admits any tape alphabet,
with binary digits embedded into its dedicated counter tape.

## Design (decisions 12.7.1–12.7.6, user 2026-10-10)

* **Symbol transport** (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.mapWorkSymbols`). A machine
  conjugated by a permutation of the work-tape alphabet runs as the
  original, cell for cell, from every configuration. This is the generic
  route of decision 12.7.4, so the decrement proof never copies the
  increment proof.
* **C1, decrement** (`Turing.decrementTM`). It is defined as
  `Turing.incrementTM` conjugated by bit complement, and its framed
  contracts are the §12.6 increment contracts transported.
* **C2, the counter-driven host** (`Turing.counterLoopTM`). The body's `k`
  tapes are embedded by R1 along `Fin.castSucc`, and the counter is the
  dedicated last tape (12.7.1). Arriving at the anchor starts a decrement,
  and success re-enters the body at the anchor, with no dispatch steps.
  Underflow leaves through the live anchor `done`; reaching the optional
  designated body exit leaves through the live anchor `escape` (12.7.2).
  A consumer branches on the two exits with `Turing.seamCompTM`; with no
  exit (`none`), `escape` is unreachable.
* **R8.0b, rich alphabets.** `Turing.counterLoopTMVia` transports the one-tape
  decrement through the symbol overlay and R1. Both generic contracts use the
  single round induction; the Bool contracts follow by identity-table agreement.
* **Round cost** (12.7.3). Each round from body configuration `c` lasts
  the **exact** time `τ c`. A round-indexed cost is the special case of
  `τ` along the orbit, and a uniform bound is the corollary
  `Turing.counterLoop_time_le`.
* **Amortized time** (12.7.6). The total is stated exactly over the whole
  run. The decrements' share, `Turing.counterOverhead`, is at most four
  steps per round plus one sweep of the counter.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.mapWorkSymbols` — conjugation by a work-tape symbol
  permutation, with `Turing.Action.mapWorkSymbols` and
  `Turing.Cfg.mapWorkSymbols`.
* `Turing.decFixed`, `Turing.decrementTM` — fixed-width decrement, as a
  word function and as a machine.
* `Turing.counterWord`, `Turing.counterOverhead` — the counter after `r`
  decrements, and the exact cost of the first `r` decrements, valid as a
  physical cost for `r ≤ value + 1` (the counter word freezes at zero,
  while the machine wraps).
* `Turing.CounterLoopState`, `Turing.counterLoopTM`,
  `Turing.counterLoopCfg`, `Turing.counterLoopOrbit` — the host, its
  configurations, and the body's round-start configurations.
* `Turing.lastEmb`, `Turing.counterLoopTMVia` — the last-tape embedding and
  the rich-alphabet counter host.
* `Turing.expandTM` — the expansion (§12.8, R8.6): the counter loop whose
  round is the advancing writer `Turing.writeAdvTM`.

## Main results


* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.mapWorkSymbols_runFrom` — symbol transport.
* `Turing.decrementTM_run_succ_ofCfg`, `Turing.decrementTM_run_underflow_ofCfg`
  — the framed decrement contracts, in the §12.6 shape.
* `Turing.counterWord_length`, `Turing.counterWord_value`,
  `Turing.counterOverhead_le_of_le`, `Turing.counterOverhead_le` — counter
  arithmetic, including the amortized bound.
* `Turing.counterLoopTM_run_done`, `Turing.counterLoopTM_run_escape` — the
  host's exact whole-run contracts, with no earlier exit, the counter
  head's range, and the body heads' trajectory.
* `Turing.counterLoopTMVia_run_done`, `Turing.counterLoopTMVia_run_escape` —
  the rich-alphabet whole-run contracts, preserving the arbitrary rich frame.
* `Turing.counterLoop_time_le` — the uniform per-round bound.
* `Turing.expandTM_run_ofCfg` — the expansion writes its pattern once per
  counter unit, contiguously, at exact time (modulo the advancing writer, §12.8).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§3.1–§3.2 and §4.1: the hierarchy
  arguments run a universal machine for a bounded number of steps under a
  step counter; this file is that counter as a reusable machine.)

**Fill appendix (§12.7).** All ten contracts are proved. Decrement is transported from increment once; `counter_rounds` is the single
round induction used by both host contracts. Its final state is unrestricted,
so it covers returning prefixes and the last escaping round with the same
trajectory invariant. The amortization proofs use the audit's bit-count
potential, as recorded in their fill appendices.
-/

namespace Turing

section SymbolTransport

variable {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type*}

/-- Rename the symbols an action writes on its work tapes along an
equivalence. Input movement, output and successor state are unchanged. -/
def Action.mapWorkSymbols (e : Symbol ≃ Symbol) (a : Action k Symbol State) :
    Action k Symbol State where
  inputTape := a.inputTape
  workTapes := fun j => ((a.workTapes j).1.map (Option.map e), (a.workTapes j).2)
  output := a.output
  state := a.state

/-- Rename every work-tape cell of a configuration along an equivalence;
blank cells stay blank. -/
def Cfg.mapWorkSymbols {input : List Symbol} (e : Symbol ≃ Symbol)
    (c : Cfg k Symbol State input) : Cfg k Symbol State input :=
  { c with workTapes := fun j p => (c.workTapes j p).map e }

/-- Conjugate a machine by a work-tape symbol permutation: read the work
tapes through `e.symm` and write through `e`. The input tape and the output
are not renamed. -/
def MultiTapeTM.mapWorkSymbols (M : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (e : Symbol ≃ Symbol) : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State where
  q₀ := M.q₀
  tr := fun q inp work => (M.tr q inp fun j => (work j).map e.symm).mapWorkSymbols e

/-- One step commutes with work-symbol conjugation, including writes into the frame.
**Proof sketch.** Inverse decoding cancels the equivalence at each read.
On the written cell the renamed update stores the renamed symbol; off that
cell the original tape is retained. The remaining configuration fields agree. -/
private lemma counter_work_step (M : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State) (e : Symbol ≃ Symbol)
    {input : List Symbol} (d : Cfg k Symbol State input) :
    (M.mapWorkSymbols e).step (d.mapWorkSymbols e) = (M.step d).mapWorkSymbols e := by
  cases hs : d.state with
  | none => simp [MultiTapeTM.step, Cfg.mapWorkSymbols, hs]
  | some s =>
    have reads : (fun j => ((d.workTapeSymbols j).map e).map e.symm) =
        d.workTapeSymbols := by
      funext j
      cases d.workTapeSymbols j <;> simp
    simp only [MultiTapeTM.step, Cfg.mapWorkSymbols, hs]
    change ((M.tr s d.inputSymbol (fun j =>
        ((d.workTapeSymbols j).map e).map e.symm)).mapWorkSymbols e).apply
        (d.mapWorkSymbols e) = _
    rw [reads]
    apply Cfg.ext <;> try rfl
    funext j p
    simp only [Action.apply, Action.mapWorkSymbols, Cfg.mapWorkSymbols]
    cases hw : (M.tr s d.inputSymbol d.workTapeSymbols).workTapes j |>.1 with
    | none => rfl
    | some v =>
      simp only [Option.map_some]
      by_cases hp : p = d.workTapePos j
      · subst p; simp
      · simp [Function.update_of_ne hp]

/-- **Symbol transport** (design §12.7, decision 12.7.4). From every
configuration and at every time, the conjugated machine runs as the original
with every work-tape cell renamed.

**Proof sketch.** One step: the conjugate reads `e.symm (e s) = s`, so it
chooses the original's action; writing renamed symbols commutes with
`Function.update`; heads, input position, output and state are copied. Then
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_comm_of_step` iterates. -/
theorem MultiTapeTM.mapWorkSymbols_runFrom (M : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
    (e : Symbol ≃ Symbol) {input : List Symbol} (c : Cfg k Symbol State input)
    (t : ℕ) :
    (M.mapWorkSymbols e).runFrom (c.mapWorkSymbols e) t =
      (M.runFrom c t).mapWorkSymbols e := by
  exact MultiTapeTM.runFrom_comm_of_step (fun d => d.mapWorkSymbols e)
    (counter_work_step M e) c t

end SymbolTransport

/-! ## C1 — decrement -/

/-- Little-endian fixed-width binary decrement with explicit underflow, the
mirror of `Turing.incFixed`: `decFixed w` is the predecessor word of the same
length, or `none` when `w` is all `false`, that is, has value zero. Width zero
underflows immediately. -/
def decFixed : List Bool → Option (List Bool)
  | [] => none
  | true :: rest => some (false :: rest)
  | false :: rest => (decFixed rest).map (true :: ·)

/-- Complement exchanges the word-level carry and borrow recursions. -/
private lemma counter_dec_complement (w : List Bool) :
    decFixed w = (incFixed (w.map not)).map (List.map not) := by
  induction w with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b w ih =>
    cases b <;> simp [decFixed, incFixed, ih, List.map_map, Function.comp_def]

/-- Complementing work cells twice restores an arbitrary configuration. -/
private lemma counter_complement_twice {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (d : Cfg k Bool S x) :
    (d.mapWorkSymbols Equiv.boolNot).mapWorkSymbols Equiv.boolNot = d := by
  apply Cfg.ext <;> try rfl
  funext j p
  simp [Cfg.mapWorkSymbols, Option.map_map, Function.comp_def]

/-- Complementation of a buffered word preserves its blank delimiters. -/
private lemma counter_buffer_complement (w : List Bool) (p : ℤ) :
    FinTM.bufferTape (w.map not) p = (FinTM.bufferTape w p).map not := by
  exact FinTM.bufferTape_map Equiv.boolNot.toEmbedding w p

/-- **R3, decrement** (design §12.7, C1). In-place little-endian fixed-width
binary decrement on tape `i`. The borrow pass flips `false` cells to `true`
moving right. The first `true` flips to `false` and selects the success
verdict. Running off the width (all `false`, value zero) selects the
underflow verdict, leaving the wrapped all-`true` word. The return pass
carries the verdict to the live `done` anchor at the origin.

It is defined as `Turing.incrementTM` conjugated by bit complement, so its
contracts are the increment's, transported by
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.mapWorkSymbols_runFrom`. -/
def decrementTM (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) : MultiTapeTM k Bool FlagPhase :=
  (incrementTM k i).mapWorkSymbols Equiv.boolNot

/-- Every decrement run is one complemented increment run, including its frame. -/
private lemma counter_decrement_run {k : ℕ} {x : List Bool} (i : Fin k)
    (d : Cfg k Bool FlagPhase x) (t : ℕ) :
    (decrementTM k i).runFrom d t =
      ((incrementTM k i).runFrom (d.mapWorkSymbols Equiv.boolNot) t).mapWorkSymbols
        Equiv.boolNot := by
  simpa only [decrementTM, counter_complement_twice] using
    (incrementTM k i).mapWorkSymbols_runFrom Equiv.boolNot
      (d.mapWorkSymbols Equiv.boolNot) t

/-- **Decrement, framed success with exact borrow cost** (design §12.7, C1;
the mirror of `Turing.incrementTM_run_succ_ofCfg`). Let the delimited word `w`
on tape `i` have a predecessor at its width, `decFixed w = some v`, and let
`q = (w.takeWhile not).length` be its number of leading `false` cells. Then
the routine reaches the success anchor at exactly `2q + 2` and not earlier,
with the word interval holding `v` and everything else unchanged. Up to the
exit the head stays within `[pos - 1, pos + q]`.

**Proof sketch.** Complement the configuration's work tapes. The result
carries `w.map not`, whose successor is `v.map not` (`decFixed` is `incFixed`
conjugated by `not`) and whose `true` prefix has length `q`. Apply
`Turing.incrementTM_run_succ_ofCfg`, transport back by
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.mapWorkSymbols_runFrom`, and use that complementing
twice is the identity and that `FinTM.bufferTape` commutes with `map not`. -/
theorem decrementTM_run_succ_ofCfg {k : ℕ} {x : List Bool} (i : Fin k)
    (w v : List Bool) (hv : decFixed w = some v) (d : Cfg k Bool FlagPhase x)
    (hstate : d.state = some FlagPhase.run)
    (hw : ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ (w.length : ℤ) →
      d.workTapes i (d.workTapePos i + p) = FinTM.bufferTape w p) :
    (decrementTM k i).runFrom d (2 * (w.takeWhile not).length + 2) =
        { d with
          state := some (FlagPhase.done true)
          workTapes := fun j q =>
            if j = i ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + (w.length : ℤ)
              then FinTM.bufferTape v (q - d.workTapePos j)
            else d.workTapes j q } ∧
      (∀ t < 2 * (w.takeWhile not).length + 2, ∀ b : Bool,
        ((decrementTM k i).runFrom d t).state ≠ some (FlagPhase.done b)) ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ 2 * (w.takeWhile not).length + 2 →
        if j = i then
          ((decrementTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈
            Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - 1)
              (d.workTapePos j + ((w.takeWhile not).length : ℤ))
        else ((decrementTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
  have hv' : incFixed (w.map not) = some (v.map not) := by
    have h := congrArg (Option.map (List.map not)) hv
    simpa [counter_dec_complement, Option.map_map, List.map_map, Function.comp_def] using h
  have hf : ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ ((w.map not).length : ℤ) →
      (d.mapWorkSymbols Equiv.boolNot).workTapes i
        ((d.mapWorkSymbols Equiv.boolNot).workTapePos i + p) =
          FinTM.bufferTape (w.map not) p := by
    intro p hl hr
    simpa [Cfg.mapWorkSymbols, counter_buffer_complement] using
      congrArg (Option.map not) (hw p hl (by simpa using hr))
  have hp : ((w.map not).takeWhile id).length = (w.takeWhile not).length := by
    simp [List.takeWhile_map, Function.comp_def]
  obtain ⟨he, hc, hh⟩ := incrementTM_run_succ_ofCfg i (w.map not) (v.map not)
    hv' (d.mapWorkSymbols Equiv.boolNot) hstate hf
  rw [hp] at he hc hh
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [counter_decrement_run, he]
    apply Cfg.ext <;> try rfl
    funext j p
    simp only [Cfg.mapWorkSymbols, List.length_map]
    split_ifs <;> simp [counter_buffer_complement, Option.map_map, Function.comp_def]
  · simpa only [counter_decrement_run, Cfg.mapWorkSymbols] using hc
  · simpa only [counter_decrement_run, Cfg.mapWorkSymbols] using hh

/-- **Decrement, framed underflow** (design §12.7, C1; the mirror of
`Turing.incrementTM_run_overflow_ofCfg`). If the delimited word `w` on tape
`i` has no predecessor at its width (`decFixed w = none`, that is, it is all
`false`), the routine reaches the underflow anchor at exactly `2|w| + 2` and
not earlier. The word interval then holds `|w|` copies of `true`, and
everything else is unchanged. Up to the exit the head stays within
`[pos - 1, pos + |w|]`.

**Proof sketch.** As the success case, through
`Turing.incrementTM_run_overflow_ofCfg`: the complemented word is all `true`,
so `incFixed` overflows, and the wrapped all-`false` word complements back to
all `true`. -/
theorem decrementTM_run_underflow_ofCfg {k : ℕ} {x : List Bool} (i : Fin k)
    (w : List Bool) (hv : decFixed w = none) (d : Cfg k Bool FlagPhase x)
    (hstate : d.state = some FlagPhase.run)
    (hw : ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ (w.length : ℤ) →
      d.workTapes i (d.workTapePos i + p) = FinTM.bufferTape w p) :
    (decrementTM k i).runFrom d (2 * w.length + 2) =
        { d with
          state := some (FlagPhase.done false)
          workTapes := fun j q =>
            if j = i ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + (w.length : ℤ)
              then FinTM.bufferTape (List.replicate w.length true) (q - d.workTapePos j)
            else d.workTapes j q } ∧
      (∀ t < 2 * w.length + 2, ∀ b : Bool,
        ((decrementTM k i).runFrom d t).state ≠ some (FlagPhase.done b)) ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ 2 * w.length + 2 →
        if j = i then
          ((decrementTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈
            Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - 1) (d.workTapePos j + (w.length : ℤ))
        else ((decrementTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
  have hv' : incFixed (w.map not) = none := by
    simpa only [counter_dec_complement, Option.map_eq_none_iff] using hv
  obtain ⟨he, hc, hh⟩ := incrementTM_run_overflow_ofCfg i (w.map not) hv'
    (d.mapWorkSymbols Equiv.boolNot) hstate (by
      intro p hl hr
      change (d.workTapes i (d.workTapePos i + p)).map Equiv.boolNot = _
      rw [hw p hl (by simpa using hr), counter_buffer_complement]
      rfl)
  simp only [List.length_map] at he hc hh
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [counter_decrement_run, he]
    apply Cfg.ext <;> try rfl
    funext j p
    have hb := counter_buffer_complement (List.replicate w.length false)
      (p - d.workTapePos j)
    simp only [Cfg.mapWorkSymbols]
    split_ifs
    · simpa using hb.symm
    · simp [Option.map_map, Function.comp_def]
  · intro t ht b
    exact (hc t ht b) ∘ (by simp only [counter_decrement_run, Cfg.mapWorkSymbols]; exact id)
  · simpa only [counter_decrement_run, Cfg.mapWorkSymbols] using hh

/-! ## Counter arithmetic -/

/-- The counter word after `r` decrements. A decrement at value zero leaves
the word unchanged here; the machine's underflow wrap is stated in the host
contract. -/
def counterWord (w : List Bool) (r : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  (fun u => (decFixed u).getD u)^[r] w

/-- The cost sum of the first `r` decrements along the frozen word orbit
`Turing.counterWord`: the decrement of the word `u` costs
`2 * (u.takeWhile not).length + 2`, which is also the underflow cost
`2|u| + 2` when `u` is all `false`. Because `counterWord` freezes at value
zero while the machine wraps on underflow, the sum equals the physical
countdown's cost only through its first underflow, that is for
`r ≤ value + 1`. That range covers every use in this file (§12.7 statement
gate, SC-1). -/
def counterOverhead (w : List Bool) (r : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.range r, (2 * ((counterWord w j).takeWhile not).length + 2)

/-- A borrow either detects an all-false word or preserves width, subtracts one,
and changes the true-bit potential by its false-prefix length.
**Proof sketch.** Induct on the word. A true low bit stops the borrow; a false
low bit propagates it and gains one true bit. -/
private lemma counter_dec_spec (w : List Bool) :
    match decFixed w with
    | none => w = List.replicate w.length false
    | some v => v.length = w.length ∧
        Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) = Nat.ofDigits 2 (v.map Bool.toNat) + 1 ∧
        v.count true + 1 = w.count true + (w.takeWhile not).length := by
  induction w with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b w ih =>
    cases b with
    | true => simp [decFixed, Nat.ofDigits_cons, Nat.add_comm]
    | false =>
      cases hd : decFixed w with
      | none =>
        simp only [hd] at ih
        simpa [decFixed, hd, List.replicate_succ] using congrArg (false :: ·) ih
      | some v =>
        simp only [hd] at ih
        rcases ih with ⟨hl, hv, hc⟩
        simp [decFixed, hd, Nat.ofDigits_cons, hl]
        omega

/-- The next frozen counter word is obtained by one optional decrement. -/
private lemma counter_word_succ (w : List Bool) (r : ℕ) :
    counterWord w (r + 1) = (decFixed (counterWord w r)).getD (counterWord w r) :=
  Function.iterate_succ_apply' _ _ _

/-- Underflow occurs exactly at binary value zero, including padded words. -/
private lemma counter_dec_zero (w : List Bool) :
    decFixed w = none ↔ Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) = 0 := by
  have hs := counter_dec_spec w
  cases hd : decFixed w with
  | none =>
    simp only [hd] at hs
    simp only [true_iff]
    conv_lhs => rw [hs]
    simp
  | some v =>
    simp only [hd] at hs
    simp only [reduceCtorEq, false_iff]
    omega

/-- Decrements preserve the counter's width.

**Proof sketch.** `decFixed` preserves length, by induction on the word, and
`Option.getD` keeps the word otherwise; induct on `r`. -/
theorem counterWord_length (w : List Bool) (r : ℕ) :
    (counterWord w r).length = w.length := by
  induction r with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ r ih =>
    rw [counter_word_succ]
    have hs := counter_dec_spec (counterWord w r)
    cases hd : decFixed (counterWord w r) with
    | none => simpa [hd] using ih
    | some v =>
      rw [hd] at hs
      simpa [hd] using hs.1.trans ih

/-- Each of the first `value w` decrements lowers the little-endian value by
one.

**Proof sketch.** For a word of positive value, `decFixed` succeeds and its
result has value one less, by induction on the word: a leading `true`
loses weight one, and a leading `false` borrows from the rest with weight
two. Induct on `r`. -/
theorem counterWord_value (w : List Bool) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : r ≤ Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)) :
    Nat.ofDigits 2 ((counterWord w r).map Bool.toNat) =
      Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) - r := by
  induction r with
  | zero => simp [counterWord]
  | succ r ih =>
    have hi := ih (by omega)
    have hs := counter_dec_spec (counterWord w r)
    rw [counter_word_succ]
    cases hb : decFixed (counterWord w r) with
    | none =>
      have hz := (counter_dec_zero _).mp hb
      omega
    | some v =>
      simp only [hb] at hs
      simp only [Option.getD_some]
      omega

/-- Before exhaustion, the physical predecessor is the next frozen word. -/
private lemma counter_word_decrement (w : List Bool) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : r < Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)) :
    decFixed (counterWord w r) = some (counterWord w (r + 1)) := by
  have hv := counterWord_value w r (by omega)
  rw [counter_word_succ]
  cases hd : decFixed (counterWord w r) with
  | none => have hz := (counter_dec_zero _).mp hd; omega
  | some v => rfl

/-- Successful borrow costs telescope against twice the number of true bits.
**Proof sketch.** At each step the borrow specification equates the new
potential plus four with the old potential plus the exact decrement cost.
Add this equality to the induction hypothesis. -/
private lemma counter_potential (w : List Bool) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : r ≤ Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)) :
    counterOverhead w r + 2 * w.count true =
      4 * r + 2 * (counterWord w r).count true := by
  induction r with
  | zero => simp [counterOverhead, counterWord]
  | succ r ih =>
    have hi := ih (by omega)
    have hs := counter_dec_spec (counterWord w r)
    rw [counter_word_decrement w r (by omega)] at hs
    simp only [counterOverhead, Finset.sum_range_succ]
    change (counterOverhead w r + (2 * (List.takeWhile not (counterWord w r)).length + 2)) +
      2 * w.count true = 4 * (r + 1) + 2 * (counterWord w (r + 1)).count true
    omega

/-- **Prefix amortization.** The first `r` decrements, for `r` at most the
counter's value, cost at most `4r + 2|w|`.

**Proof sketch.** The `j`th decrement acts on a word of value `n - j`
(`Turing.counterWord_value`), where `n` is the counter's value, and its
`false` prefix is the number of trailing zero bits of that value. Summed over
`r` consecutive values below `2^|w|`, the trailing zeros total
`ν₂(r!) + ν₂(binom) ≤ (r - 1) + (|w| - 1)` by Legendre and Kummer, so the
cost is at most `4r + 2|w| - 4` once `r ≥ 1`.

**Fill proof appendix.** The binding statement-gate route replaces the
number-theoretic sketch above by the exact telescoping identity proved in
`counter_potential`. Twice the count of true bits is the potential; its
terminal value is bounded by twice the preserved word length. -/
theorem counterOverhead_le_of_le (w : List Bool) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : r ≤ Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)) :
    counterOverhead w r ≤ 4 * r + 2 * w.length := by
  have hp := counter_potential w r hr
  have hc : (counterWord w r).count true ≤ w.length :=
    (List.count_le_length).trans_eq (counterWord_length w r)
  omega

/-- At exhaustion the fixed-width word is all false, retaining any padding. -/
private lemma counter_word_exhausted (w : List Bool) :
    counterWord w (Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)) =
      List.replicate w.length false := by
  have hz := counterWord_value w (Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)) le_rfl
  simp only [Nat.sub_self] at hz
  have hs := counter_dec_spec (counterWord w (Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)))
  rw [(counter_dec_zero _).mpr hz] at hs
  simpa only [counterWord_length] using hs

/-- **Whole-run amortization** (design §12.7, decision 12.7.6). Counting a
counter of value `n` down to zero and through the final underflow costs at
most `4n + 2|w| + 2`.

**Proof sketch.** The successful decrements act on the values `n, …, 1`,
whose trailing zeros sum to `n - s₂(n) ≤ n` (Legendre), so they cost at most
`4n`. The final word is all `false` (`Turing.counterWord_value`), so the
underflow sweep costs `2|w| + 2` (`Turing.counterWord_length`).

**Fill proof appendix.** Use `counter_potential` at exhaustion, where the
remaining true-bit count is zero, then add the full underflow sweep.
No Legendre or Kummer theorem is used. -/
theorem counterOverhead_le (w : List Bool) :
    counterOverhead w (Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) + 1) ≤
      4 * Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) + 2 * w.length + 2 := by
  have hp := counter_potential w (Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)) le_rfl
  rw [counter_word_exhausted] at hp
  simp [List.count_replicate] at hp
  have hs : counterOverhead w (Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat) + 1) =
      counterOverhead w (Nat.ofDigits 2 (w.map Bool.toNat)) + (2 * w.length + 2) := by
    simp [counterOverhead, Finset.sum_range_succ, counter_word_exhausted]
  omega

/-! ## C2 — the counter-driven host -/

/-- Control of the counter-driven host (design §12.7, C2): a body state, a
decrement phase, or one of the two live exit anchors. -/
inductive CounterLoopState (S : Type) where
  /-- running the body -/
  | body (s : S)
  /-- running the decrement on the counter tape -/
  | dec (f : FlagPhase)
  /-- the live exit anchor after the counter underflows -/
  | done
  /-- the live exit anchor after the body reaches its designated exit -/
  | escape
deriving DecidableEq

instance counterLoopStateFintype (S : Type) [Fintype S] :
    Fintype (CounterLoopState S) := derive_fintype% _

/-- Where a body transition lands in the host. Arriving at the anchor `a`
starts the next decrement; arriving at the designated exit leaves through
`escape`; every other body state is kept. -/
def counterLoopRedirect {S : Type} [DecidableEq S] (a : S) (exit : Option S)
    (s : S) : CounterLoopState S :=
  if s = a then .dec .run else if exit = some s then .escape else .body s

/-- Where a decrement transition lands in the host. The success anchor
re-enters the body at `a`, the underflow anchor is the host's `done`, and the
working phases are kept. -/
def counterLoopDecExit {S : Type} (a : S) : FlagPhase → CounterLoopState S
  | .done true => .body a
  | .done false => .done
  | f => .dec f

/-- **C2, the counter-driven loop host** (design §12.7). The body `M` runs on
the first `k` tapes, embedded by `Turing.embedEmitTM` along `Fin.castSucc`
with its emissions forwarded, and the counter is the last tape. The host
starts with a decrement. Each successful decrement re-enters the body at the
anchor `a`, and each arrival at `a` starts the next decrement, with no
dispatch steps in between. Underflow leaves through the live anchor `done`;
reaching the optional exit leaves through the live anchor `escape`. Both
anchors are stationary. -/
def counterLoopTM {k : ℕ} {S : Type} [DecidableEq S] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool S)
    (a : S) (exit : Option S) : MultiTapeTM (k + 1) Bool (CounterLoopState S) where
  q₀ := .dec .run
  tr := fun q inp work =>
    match q with
    | .body s =>
      ((embedEmitTM Fin.castSuccEmb M).tr s inp work).mapState (counterLoopRedirect a exit)
    | .dec f =>
      ((decrementTM (k + 1) (Fin.last k)).tr f inp work).mapState (counterLoopDecExit a)
    | .done => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some .done⟩
    | .escape => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some .escape⟩

/-- Select the last host tape as a one-tape bank (design §12.8a, R8.0b).
**Proof sketch.** The singleton domain makes the constant last-tape map injective. -/
def lastEmb (k : ℕ) : Fin 1 ↪ Fin (k + 1) :=
  ⟨fun _ => Fin.last k, fun a b _ => Subsingleton.elim a b⟩

/-- Run a rich-alphabet body with an embedded binary counter on the last tape
(design §12.8a, R8.0b).
**Proof sketch.** R1 forwards the body and the symbol-lifted one-tape decrement;
the existing redirections connect the phases without dispatch steps. -/
def counterLoopTMVia {k : ℕ} {Γ S : Type} [DecidableEq S] [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ)
    (M : MultiTapeTM k Γ S) (a : S) (exit : Option S) :
    MultiTapeTM (k + 1) Γ (CounterLoopState S) where
  q₀ := .dec .run
  tr := fun q inp work =>
    match q with
    | .body s =>
      ((embedEmitTM Fin.castSuccEmb M).tr s inp work).mapState (counterLoopRedirect a exit)
    | .dec f =>
      ((embedEmitTM (lastEmb k) ((decrementTM 1 0).liftSymbols e)).tr f inp work).mapState
        (counterLoopDecExit a)
    | .done => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some .done⟩
    | .escape => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some .escape⟩

/-- A host configuration with host state `q`: the body configuration `c` on
the first `k` tapes (its own state field is ignored), the counter tape `ct`
with its head at `cp` as the last tape, and the body's output as the host's
output. It is the R1 transport `Turing.embedEmitCfg` along `Fin.castSucc`,
with the counter as the ambient frame. -/
def counterLoopCfg {k : ℕ} {Symbol S : Type} {x : List Symbol}
    (q : Option (CounterLoopState S)) (c : Cfg k Symbol S x)
    (ct : ℤ → Option Symbol) (cp : ℤ) : Cfg (k + 1) Symbol (CounterLoopState S) x :=
  { (embedEmitCfg Fin.castSuccEmb (fun _ => ct) (fun _ => cp) [] c).mapState
      CounterLoopState.body with state := q }

/-- The body configurations at the starts of successive rounds: round `r`
starts from `counterLoopOrbit M τ c r`, and a round from `c` lasts `τ c`
steps. -/
def counterLoopOrbit {k : ℕ} {Symbol S : Type} {x : List Symbol} (M : MultiTapeTM k Symbol S)
    (τ : Cfg k Symbol S x → ℕ) (c : Cfg k Symbol S x) (r : ℕ) : Cfg k Symbol S x :=
  (fun c => M.runFrom c (τ c))^[r] c

/-! ### Shared phase and prefix invariants -/

/-- The host layout over any tape alphabet.
**Proof sketch.** R1 identifies the selected body bank and the last-tape frame. -/
private lemma counter_layout {k : ℕ} {Symbol S : Type} {x : List Symbol}
    (q : Option (CounterLoopState S)) (c : Cfg k Symbol S x)
    (ct : ℤ → Option Symbol) (cp : ℤ) :
    counterLoopCfg q c ct cp =
      ⟨q, c.inputPos, Fin.lastCases ct c.workTapes,
        Fin.lastCases cp c.workTapePos, c.output⟩ := by
  have hf := (embedEmitTM_frame Fin.castSuccEmb
    (⟨(), fun _ _ _ => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, none⟩⟩ : MultiTapeTM k Symbol Unit)
    (fun _ => ct) (fun _ => cp) [] (c.mapState (fun _ => ())) 0).1
    (Fin.last k) (by rintro ⟨i, hi⟩; exact Fin.castSucc_ne_last i hi)
  apply Cfg.ext <;> try rfl
  · funext j
    refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun i => ?_) j
    · simpa only [counterLoopCfg, Cfg.mapState, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero,
        Fin.lastCases_last] using hf.1
    · simpa only [counterLoopCfg, Cfg.mapState, Fin.lastCases_castSucc] using
        embedEmitCfg_selected_tape Fin.castSuccEmb (fun _ => ct) (fun _ => cp) [] c i
  · funext j
    refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun i => ?_) j
    · simpa only [counterLoopCfg, Cfg.mapState, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero,
        Fin.lastCases_last] using hf.2
    · simpa only [counterLoopCfg, Cfg.mapState, Fin.lastCases_castSucc] using
        embedEmitCfg_selected_pos Fin.castSuccEmb (fun _ => ct) (fun _ => cp) [] c i

/-- **The counter-loop host layout** (design §12.7; public since the §12.8 fill): the
host configuration is the body bank followed by its counter tape.

**Proof sketch.** The body tapes are R1's selected tapes (`Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_tape`,
`_pos`); the counter tape is its frame (`Turing.embedEmitTM_frame` at time `0`).

**Re-derivation appendix (R8.0b).** Instantiate the generic private layout at the Bool alphabet. -/
theorem counter_cfg_eq {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (q : Option (CounterLoopState S)) (c : Cfg k Bool S x)
    (ct : ℤ → Option Bool) (cp : ℤ) :
    counterLoopCfg q c ct cp =
      ⟨q, c.inputPos, Fin.lastCases ct c.workTapes,
        Fin.lastCases cp c.workTapePos, c.output⟩ :=
  counter_layout q c ct cp

/-- Injective successor redirection for the decrement's five controls. -/
private lemma counter_dec_injective {S : Type} (a : S) :
    Function.Injective (counterLoopDecExit a) := by
  intro f g h
  cases f <;> cases g <;> (try casesm* Bool) <;> simp_all [counterLoopDecExit]

/-- Anchor priority still gives an injective body-state redirection. -/
private lemma counter_redirect_injective {S : Type} [DecidableEq S]
    (a : S) (exit : Option S) : Function.Injective (counterLoopRedirect a exit) := by
  intro s t h
  by_cases hs : s = a
  · subst s
    by_cases ht : t = a
    · exact ht.symm
    · simp only [counterLoopRedirect, ht, if_false] at h
      split_ifs at h
  · by_cases ht : t = a
    · subst t; simp only [counterLoopRedirect, hs, if_false] at h
      split_ifs at h
    · simp only [counterLoopRedirect, hs, ht, if_false] at h
      split_ifs at h <;> simp_all

/-- Common trajectory data for a finite host segment, with a chosen set of
permitted body-head vectors. -/
private def counterSpan {k : ℕ} {Γ S : Type} {x : List Γ}
    (H : MultiTapeTM (k + 1) Γ (CounterLoopState S))
    (z : Cfg (k + 1) Γ (CounterLoopState S) x) (t : ℕ) (cp : ℤ) (width : ℕ)
    (R : (Fin k → ℤ) → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ u < t, (H.runFrom z u).state ≠ some .done ∧
    (H.runFrom z u).state ≠ some .escape) ∧
  (∀ u ≤ t, (H.runFrom z u).workTapePos (Fin.last k) ∈
    Finset.Icc (cp - 1) (cp + (width : ℤ))) ∧
  (∀ u ≤ t, R (fun j => (H.runFrom z u).workTapePos j.castSucc))

/-- Adjacent segments concatenate their cuts and trajectory bounds.
**Proof sketch.** Split a queried time at the first segment's length and
use run addition on the suffix. The two head-vector relations imply the
requested relation separately. -/
private lemma counter_span_append {k : ℕ} {Γ S : Type} {x : List Γ}
    (H : MultiTapeTM (k + 1) Γ (CounterLoopState S))
    (z : Cfg (k + 1) Γ (CounterLoopState S) x) (s t : ℕ) (cp : ℤ) (width : ℕ)
    (R₁ R₂ R : (Fin k → ℤ) → Prop)
    (h₁ : counterSpan H z s cp width R₁)
    (h₂ : counterSpan H (H.runFrom z s) t cp width R₂)
    (hr₁ : ∀ p, R₁ p → R p) (hr₂ : ∀ p, R₂ p → R p) :
    counterSpan H z (s + t) cp width R := by
  have suffix (u : ℕ) (hu : s ≤ u) :
      H.runFrom z u = H.runFrom (H.runFrom z s) (u - s) := by
    rw [← H.runFrom_add, Nat.add_sub_of_le hu]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro u hu
    by_cases hs : u < s
    · exact h₁.1 u hs
    · rw [suffix u (by omega)]; exact h₂.1 (u - s) (by omega)
  · intro u hu
    by_cases hs : u ≤ s
    · exact h₁.2.1 u hs
    · rw [suffix u (by omega)]; exact h₂.2.1 (u - s) (by omega)
  · intro u hu
    by_cases hs : u ≤ s
    · exact hr₁ _ (h₁.2.2 u hs)
    · rw [suffix u (by omega)]; exact hr₂ _ (h₂.2.2 (u - s) (by omega))

/-- A width-preserving overwrite of just the counter word interval. -/
private def counterPatch {Γ : Type} (ct : ℤ → Option Γ) (cp : ℤ) (w : List Γ) : ℤ → Option Γ :=
  fun q => if cp ≤ q ∧ q < cp + (w.length : ℤ)
    then FinTM.bufferTape w (q - cp) else ct q

/-- Equal-width patches overwrite the same interval, preserving the original frame. -/
private lemma counter_patch_twice {Γ : Type} (ct : ℤ → Option Γ) (cp : ℤ) (u v : List Γ)
    (hv : v.length = u.length) :
    counterPatch (counterPatch ct cp u) cp v = counterPatch ct cp v := by
  funext q
  simp only [counterPatch, hv]
  split_ifs <;> rfl

/-- Replacing a framed word by an equal-width word keeps both blank delimiters. -/
private lemma counter_patch_frame {Γ : Type} (w v : List Γ) (ct : ℤ → Option Γ) (cp : ℤ)
    (hv : v.length = w.length)
    (hw : ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ (w.length : ℤ) →
      ct (cp + p) = FinTM.bufferTape w p) :
    ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ (v.length : ℤ) →
      counterPatch ct cp v (cp + p) = FinTM.bufferTape v p := by
  intro p hl hr
  by_cases h : 0 ≤ p ∧ p < (v.length : ℤ)
  · simp [counterPatch, show cp ≤ cp + p ∧ cp + p < cp + (v.length : ℤ) by omega]
  · have hp : p = -1 ∨ p = (v.length : ℤ) := by omega
    rcases hp with rfl | rfl
    · simp [counterPatch, hw (-1) (by omega) (by omega), FinTM.bufferTape_left]
    · simp [counterPatch, hv, hw w.length (by omega) le_rfl, FinTM.bufferTape_nat]

/-- A decrement phase uses the proved framed contract and guarded state transport.
**Proof sketch.** Decode the rich one-tape start, apply the landed success or
underflow contract, and read back through the public symbol overlay. Its input
obliviousness and absence of blank writes preserve arbitrary rich frame cells.
R1 puts this run on the last tape; injective guarded state transport supplies
the host's verdict cut and the two head trajectories. -/
private lemma counter_debit {k : ℕ} {Γ S : Type} [DecidableEq S] [DecidableEq Γ] {x : List Γ}
    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (M : MultiTapeTM k Γ S) (a : S) (exit : Option S)
    (c : Cfg k Γ S x) (w : List Bool) (ct : ℤ → Option Γ) (cp : ℤ)
    (hw : ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ (w.length : ℤ) →
      ct (cp + p) = FinTM.bufferTape (w.map e) p) :
    let cost := 2 * (w.takeWhile not).length + 2
    let v := (decFixed w).getD (List.replicate w.length true)
    let q : CounterLoopState S := if (decFixed w).isSome then .body a else .done
    (counterLoopTMVia e M a exit).runFrom (counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run)) c ct cp) cost =
      counterLoopCfg (some q) c (counterPatch ct cp (v.map e)) cp ∧
    counterSpan (counterLoopTMVia e M a exit) (counterLoopCfg (some (.dec .run)) c ct cp)
      cost cp w.length (fun p => ∀ j, p j = c.workTapePos j) := by
  let D : Cfg 1 Γ FlagPhase x :=
    ⟨some .run, c.inputPos, fun _ => ct, fun _ => cp, c.output⟩
  let z := Cfg.decodeSymbols e D
  let v := (decFixed w).getD (List.replicate w.length true)
  let cost := 2 * (w.takeWhile not).length + 2
  let N := (decrementTM 1 0).liftSymbols e
  let E := embedEmitTM (lastEmb k) N
  let bank (d : Cfg 1 Γ FlagPhase x) := embedEmitCfg (lastEmb k)
    (Fin.lastCases ct c.workTapes) (Fin.lastCases cp c.workTapePos) [] d
  have layout (d : Cfg 1 Γ FlagPhase x) : bank d =
      ⟨d.state, d.inputPos, Fin.lastCases (d.workTapes 0) c.workTapes,
        Fin.lastCases (d.workTapePos 0) c.workTapePos, d.output⟩ := by
    have frame (i : Fin k) := (embedEmitTM_frame (lastEmb k) N
      (Fin.lastCases ct c.workTapes) (Fin.lastCases cp c.workTapePos) [] d 0).1
      i.castSucc (by rintro ⟨j, hj⟩; exact Fin.castSucc_ne_last i hj.symm)
    apply Cfg.ext <;> try rfl
    · funext j
      refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun i => ?_) j
      · simpa only [bank, Fin.lastCases_last] using
          embedEmitCfg_selected_tape (lastEmb k) (Fin.lastCases ct c.workTapes)
            (Fin.lastCases cp c.workTapePos) [] d 0
      · simpa only [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Fin.lastCases_castSucc] using (frame i).1
    · funext j
